title: Chapter 1884: Duty And Personal Affection (II)
content:
Chapter 1884: Duty And Personal Affection (II)

Though contradicted, this prominent minister of Great Song, the True Radiant Cloud Envoy, showed no displeasure. He merely sighed. "Brother Jianglong is on the verge of attaining divine ability and is unlikely to have more children. Suihuan is being raised as the Li Family's eldest direct heir. He has lived up to expectations, showing the potential to attain divine abilities... Meanwhile, Suichu was born in the imperial capital. He hasn't experienced nearly as much..."

His elder brother laughed and replied bluntly, "You are being far too kind. Everyone speaks of the Li Family's three Profound Holders, of your dominance at court and my formidable prestige. But we both know that those of us who ended up here as Profound Holders... had already lost out at Moongaze Lake. We fell short.

"And is it really a good thing that Suichu was born in the imperial capital, with everyone calling him young master? He is also of the Bright Yang bloodline, yet my child has grown up in sheltered palace courtyards, without responsibilities or experience of the world. When he meets his elder cousin in the future, he will feel ashamed of his own inadequacy.

"Li Jianglong was simply lucky enough to have a child early and bring him before the Daoist Master to be named."

Li Jiangliang could find no suitable reply to his brother's words. He shook his head and said, "I hear... father went to the Western Sea."

Li Jiangxia's expression grew serious. "You certainly are well informed... Has something happened?"

Li Jiangliang smiled wryly. "What could have happened...? My wife complained in passing about the gift of that treasure. The [Heavenly Nurturing Urn] came from the Song Emperor's own destined opportunity, rather than the Yang Family's stores. And it possesses a mystic that can capture and suppress others, then extract their essence..."

He raised his brows and sighed. "You know what our father is like. He went all the way to the Western Sea and captured a demon king with two divine abilities. I hear he did not even lift a hand, using only one divine ability and one spirit treasure. He gave those rogue cultivators quite a fright."

Li Jiangxia fell silent for a while. "With father's current divine abilities, even the grand general probably wouldn't claim he could defeat him for certain!"

Li Jiangliang sighed. "Indeed. Fortunately, Western Shu has its hands full, and Northern Zhao is leaderless..."

Li Jiangxia glanced at him. "The stronger father's divine abilities become, the less those people dare act against him and the less they can do about him. Should he head to the Eastern Sea one day, you lot won't even be able to keep a clear eye on him!"

Li Jiangliang paused, then raised a hand. "They mean well."

It sounded like an explanation, but Li Jiangxia did not pursue the matter and said, "I hear the abbot of [Great Konghai Temple] has returned to his position, and there are stirrings in the Stone Pond region again..."

Li Jiangliang answered intermittently, seemingly distracted. After a long while, he asked, "Brother, have you passed through the lake since you came from the north? Did you see our father?"

Li Jiangxia paused. "Of course I passed through the lake... But Sima Yuanli was guarding it, and I saw no sign of father. Isn't he still in the Western Sea?"

The young man before him lowered his eyes slightly, yet smiled as he spoke. "This is certainly something worth celebrating. The grand general happens to have transferred me north to assist with the defenses. I will pass through the lake as well, so I can see father and offer my congratulations."

His elder brother smiled. "Then be careful! The Light of Cultivation and Martiality does not reach Tingzhou. Being stripped of your powers as a Profound Holder is hardly pleasant!"

Li Jiangliang merely smiled and left, bidding farewell as he went. He stepped into his carriage, and the crack of whips and shouted calls rang out. Shifting colors gleamed, drawing glances from passersby.

Outside, light shimmered, but the carriage's interior was dim. A woman in white sat quietly within, her expression somber. As soon as she saw him, she asked, "Well?"

Li Jiangliang shook his head. "You are overthinking it. Even if father had met my brother, he would only have offered encouragement and asked after him. At most, he might have asked about the children. Why would he discuss his gains?"

The woman's expression remained grave. "We cannot afford to be careless. Ch'ü Qian of Mount Luoxia lived in the same era as the Six Sons of Chongming and listened to teachings before a True Monarch. Aside from his immense abilities, he may well have acted on that True Monarch's instructions... It may be a scheme laid by the Lesser Yang faction.

"That is precisely why Shehu, a minor demonic creature without backing or remarkable divine abilities, managed to survive these five hundred years. Daoist Master Zhaojing's involvement may have been unexpected... but I fear there is more to it."

Li Jiangliang lowered his eyes, his voice calm. "What more could there be?"

Yang Tianyou paused. Sensing his displeasure, she lowered her voice. "Luoxia always acts at one extreme or the other. Either they perform lofty deeds befitting immortals, or they wield dharma relics and condemn others to eternal ruin. Even... Even a True Monarch faces the danger of a former exalted figure returning to contest the Five Forms. With all those dharma relics hanging over us, how can we be anything but cautious?

"Tongxuan has reserved Lesser Yang for itself. And consider the present situation. Veiled Yin has collapsed, Lesser Yin departed, Bright Yang fallen, and Lesser Yang split apart. Supreme Yin and Supreme Yang have vanished across the ages. Such matters should never be touched... especially anything involving a complete Lesser Yang."

Li Jiangliang frowned and said, "Father has already divided it up. What is there to worry about? I'll go and ask him myself. As for whether there was anything else in that cave dwelling, Luoxia knows better than anyone!"

This prominent minister of Great Song had always presented a gentle face to others, but repeatedly being made to sound out his own family had clearly crossed a line. A harsh glint flashed in his golden eyes as he spoke through gritted teeth. "They scheme against my family, yet we are the ones left worrying, terrified that something we do might displease them... If you ask me... Majestic Light is far more overbearing than Bright Yang!"

Yang Tianyou instinctively glanced at the black qi circling around them, afraid a third party might overhear. She said only, "The mainland lies within the game, where their actions can be accommodated. But the Western Sea lies outside it, where any tactic might be used. I only hoped you would ask when you went back, so Zhaojing would be on his guard..."

Li Jiangliang glanced at her and sighed. "The Daoist Master is your elder too."

Yang Tianyou realized that, in her anxiety, she had spoken carelessly and addressed Li Ximing directly by his Dao title. She looked down and said, "I spoke out of turn..."

She fell quiet for a while, then said with a hint of hurt, "My dear... I am doing this for you. Who besides me cares whether Tingzhou becomes entangled in the schemes surrounding Lesser Yang? I overheard a few words of their conversation, and now I have to ask you about it in secret..."

Li Jiangliang's brow relaxed, and his voice softened. "I know you mean well. I just... cannot help feeling angry."

Yang Tianyou wiped away her tears and leaned against his shoulder, bitterness welling within her.

In the entire Yang Family, I alone hope the King of Wei will attain the Dao and dream that we might still survive afterward... My sisters all laugh at my naivety... But am I really coveting a Bright Yang True Monarch as my father-in-law? I belong to the Underworld and must return there sooner or later. I care nothing for the rest of the Li Family. I am only trying to keep you alive...

Her tears fell like rain onto his green-purple robes, held by mana in glistening beads. Li Jiangliang gently cradled her hair and murmured, "You'er, I know what is in your heart."
